spec_match.rationale: The page demonstrates the one case selectors cannot express (first item per column) and, since 406f8e2, its narration is derived from the measured per-column groups and credits CSS Fragmentation break-margin truncation for the columns that are already flush — the copy no longer contradicts the table.

interactive.rationale: Column and item sliders, a margin-trim toggle and Re-measure rebuild the flow and a per-column measured table that groups items by rendered column.

blurb_alignment.rationale: Narration, table and the feature-index framing now tell the same story: column 1 keeps the container-edge margin that no per-column selector can remove, later columns are flush because the engine truncates margins adjoining a column break.

edge_cases.rationale: The unsupported branch distinguishes all-flush from mixed layouts and names the fragmentation rule, but the supported branch (real margin-trim on Chrome 155) is still unverifiable from Chromium 141 and should be re-measured on a shipping build.

conformance.rationale: The feature suite proves block-container behaviour well but contains no multicol assertion, so the one scenario this page exists for is unpinned — and the suite's inline assertions are separately flagged (see trim-explorer critique).

runtime_evidence.rationale: Re-verified 2026-10-04 on Chromium 141 headless via CDP (cloud fallback, no chrome-devtools-mcp): measured gaps 16/0/0 across three columns and the aria-live narration now states exactly that (1 column keeps a margin, 2 already flush via CSS Fragmentation §4.3); console clean; desktop screenshot read.

telemetry_health.rationale: Renders log and emit showcaseTelemetry.assert('multicol-measured', …) with columns, trim state and flush count.

design_system.rationale: Token colours, good/bad cells pair colour with text, amber padding band, 44px controls.

accessibility.rationale: Labelled sliders and checkbox, captioned per-column table with scoped headers, aria-live narration.

mobile_desktop_parity.rationale: 0px horizontal overflow at 360x740 DPR3 and 1280x800 over CDP; both screenshots clean.

openQuestions.title: Add a multicol assertion to the conformance suite (new assertion, additive)
openQuestions.detail: Nothing in v155/margin-trim/conformance.json exercises a multicol container, so the scenario this concept page exists for has no immutable contract. An additive assertion (column-1 first-item gap goes to zero under margin-trim: block in a column-count container) would pin it; adding new assertions is allowed, editing existing ones is not.

summary: Narration defect repaired and re-verified: commit 406f8e2 derives all three narration branches from the measured column groups, and a 2026-10-04 CDP re-check on Chromium 141 headless (cloud fallback, no chrome-devtools-mcp) at http://localhost:3000/v155/margin-trim/multicol/ shows the table (16/0/0) and the copy in agreement, with the flush columns correctly attributed to CSS Fragmentation §4.3 break-margin truncation rather than margin-trim. Console clean, no overflow. Remaining: verify the supported branch on a real Chrome 155, and a human may consider the additive multicol conformance assertion (suite untouched per the immutability rule).
